mainTopic: Nedarim 28b: the wording and exact case of the משנה's conditional vows on saplings and a garment, and how long the 'no redemption' rule lasts.
overview: The amud opens with the last words of the משנה: saplings that are קרבן 'until they are cut down,' or a garment that is קרבן 'until it is burned,' have no פדיון. The גמרא first asks why the משנה talks about 'redemption' instead of simply saying 'holy' and 'not holy.' It answers that the first clause copies the wording of the second clause, which had to use redemption language. Then אמימר explains the exact vow in the first case: 'if they are not cut down today,' and the day passed. The גמרא asks why that is not obvious, and answers that a strong wind was blowing, or for the garment, a fire was burning. The משנה teaches that even though he expected to lose the item anyway, his vow is real. Finally, the גמרא asks whether 'no redemption' lasts forever. בר פדא says the holiness keeps coming back until the saplings are cut, and after that one redemption is enough. עולא says that once they are cut, no redemption is needed at all.

steps.title: End of the משנה: no redemption
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the משנה: in the 'until they are cut / until it is burned' case, the items have no פדיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are not subject to redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of the משנה, finishing its second case. This gives the base text the גמרא is about to discuss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has two cases. In the first, 'קרבן if they are not cut down,' the items can be redeemed. In the second, 'קרבן until they are cut down / until it is burned,' the items cannot be redeemed. These final words end that second case.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption: taking holiness off an item by paying its value to הקדש

phrases.english: they are not subject to redemption.
phrases.notes: This finishes the משנה's second case: 'these saplings are קרבן until they are cut down; this garment is קרבן until it is burned.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the משנה that began on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the 'until cut / until burned' case, the items cannot be redeemed.

steps.title: Why not say 'holy and not holy'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה speaks of redemption instead of simply saying 'they are holy' and 'they are not holy.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Let the משנה teach 'they are holy' and 'they are not holy'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. The main news of the first case is that the items become holy, so why not say that directly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real חידוש of the first case is that the vow takes hold and the items become קדושות. Saying 'יש להם פדיון' seems to talk around the main point. So the גמרא suggests the משנה should have said 'קדושות' in plain words.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows the משנה
Let it teach; why didn't it teach (a challenge to wording)

phrases.english: Gemara:
But let it teach: 'they are holy and they are not holy'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's choice of words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's phrasing 'יש להם פדיון / אין להם פדיון'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The main point is whether the items are holy, so the משנה should state that directly.

steps.title: The first clause copies the wording of the second
steps.stepSummary: Because the second clause has to speak about 'no redemption,' the first clause uses the matching phrase 'there is redemption.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it wanted to teach in the latter clause 'they are not subject to redemption,' it also taught in the first clause 'they are subject to redemption.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה picked its words so that both clauses would match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second case the items ARE holy. The difference is only that they cannot be redeemed, so the משנה could not have said 'אין קדושות' there. Since the סיפא had to use redemption language, the רישא was phrased the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because (it was already using this wording)
The latter clause of a משנה
The first clause of a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the second case means the items are not holy. They are holy; they just cannot be redeemed. That is exactly why the משנה could not say 'אין קדושות.'

phrases.english: Since it wanted to teach in the latter clause
'they are not subject to redemption,'
it also taught in the first clause
'they are subject to redemption.'

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא should say 'קדושות' since that is its main point.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא could only be phrased with redemption language, so the רישא matches it.
steps.whatToRemember: An 'אַיְּידֵי' answer explains wording: one clause is phrased a certain way to match the other clause.

steps.title: What exactly did he say in his vow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exact words the person used in the first case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: what precise wording does the first case of the משנה involve? This sets up אמימר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קרבן if they are not cut down' is unclear about time. Not cut down by when? The גמרא wants to know the exact vow before it can understand the ruling.

phrases.english: How did he vow?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from wording to defining the case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact language of the conditional vow in the רישא.

steps.title: אמימר: 'If they are not cut down today'
steps.stepSummary: אמימר explains that the person said 'if they are not cut down today,' and the day ended without them being cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: When he says 'if they are not cut down today,' and the day passed and they were not cut down.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers by giving the vow a time limit: today. Once the day ends with the saplings still standing, the condition has been met.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the case is clear. The vow depends on the saplings not being cut by the end of the day. When that happens, the condition is fulfilled and the vow takes hold.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
When he says: 'if they are not cut down today,'
and the day passed and they were not cut down.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר בְּאוֹמֵר אִם אֵינָן נִקְצָצוֹת הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the exact vow.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He said 'if they are not cut down today,' and the day passed without them being cut.

steps.title: Then isn't it obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to teach this. If the condition was met, the vow obviously takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need it said? It is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אמימר's explanation: with that wording, the ruling seems too simple to need teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A conditional vow whose condition was met plainly takes hold. So what new thing is the משנה teaching by saying they are holy and can be redeemed?

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it said?

phrases.english: If so, why do I need it said?
It is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן לְמָה לִי לְמֵימַר פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אמימר's case as having no חידוש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the משנה's ruling under אמימר's reading.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the condition is fulfilled, the vow obviously takes effect, so there is nothing to teach.

steps.title: The case of a strong wind
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed for a case where a strong wind is blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where there is a strong wind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a day with a strong wind, which makes the case less simple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a strong wind blowing, the person expected the saplings to be knocked down anyway. One might think he did not seriously mean the vow. The full reasoning comes out in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed (except for this case); it is needed for this case

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where there is a strong wind.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא כְּגוֹן דְּאִיכָּא זִיקָא נְפִישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A simple conditional vow needs no teaching.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of a strong wind, where his intention is in doubt.

steps.title: But the garment is taught alongside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the wind idea fits the garment case, since a garment is not normally expected to burn.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is taught together with the garment, and is a garment standing to be burned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wind explanation from the matching garment case in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה puts the saplings and the garment side by side, so they should be the same kind of case. But nothing makes us expect a garment to burn, so where is the parallel to the strong wind?

keyTerms.meaning: But it is taught (introducing a challenge from the text)

phrases.english: But it is taught together with the garment,
and is a garment standing to be burned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the strong-wind answer from the parallel garment case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The garment case should be parallel, but a garment is not expected to burn.

steps.title: Yes, there is a fire
steps.stepSummary: The garment case is also special: there is a fire nearby.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, where there is a fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the garment case also involves a danger: a fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the wind threatens the saplings, a fire threatens the garment. So both cases in the משנה are about an item the person expects to lose.

phrases.english: Yes, where there is a fire.
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets; the corrected wording adds it.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: A garment is not expected to burn, so it does not match the wind case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The garment case involves a fire, matching the strong wind.

steps.title: The vow counts even though he expected the loss
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the חידוש: we might think he only vowed because he expected to lose the saplings, so the vow is not serious. The משנה teaches that it still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too there is a strong wind, and you might think that he expected they would not be saved, and that is why he vowed. It teaches us that the vow still counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly what the משנה is teaching in the wind (and fire) case. This closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he thought the saplings would be lost anyway, one might say he did not really mean to make them holy, so the vow should not count. The משנה, by saying 'יש להם פדיון,' teaches that they ARE holy. The vow takes hold despite his expectation.

keyTerms.meaning: He had it in mind; he assumed

steps.whatToRemember: With אמימר's wording, 'קרבן if not cut down today,' the חידוש is the strong wind or fire case. Even though he expected to lose the item, his vow is real and the item becomes holy, though it can be redeemed.

phrases.english: Here too, there is a strong wind,
and you might think that he had it in mind
that they would not be saved,
and that is why he vowed,
it teaches us.
phrases.notes: It teaches us that the vow still counts and the saplings are holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the chiddush behind the strong-wind answer, now that the garment case is resolved.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A conditional vow takes hold even when the person expected to lose the item anyway; the משנה teaches that such a vow is not dismissed as insincere.

steps.title: Does the 'no redemption' rule for the saplings last forever?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of saplings declared קרבן and asks whether 'they cannot be redeemed' is a permanent rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'These saplings are קרבן,' and so on. The גמרא asks: Can they never be redeemed, forever?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה about saplings declared holy. It asks a short question that sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says these saplings have no פדיון. The גמרא asks whether that means never, even after they are cut down. This question opens the way for בר פדא and עולא to explain what happens before and after the cutting.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering; here, a vow making the saplings holy like an offering
'Etc.'; the rest of the quote is left out

phrases.english: 'These saplings are an offering,' etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes only the start of the line in the משנה, which goes on to say these saplings cannot be redeemed.

phrases.english: And forever?
phrases.notes: He means: is it really never possible to redeem them, even after they are cut down?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic in the משנה, moving from the wind-and-fire discussion to the rule that the saplings cannot be redeemed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long does the 'no redemption' rule for the saplings last? Is it forever, or only until they are cut?

steps.title: בר פדא: Redemption does not hold before cutting; after cutting, once is enough
steps.stepSummary: בר פדא explains that while the saplings stand, every redemption is undone. Once they are cut, one redemption is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר פדא said: If he redeemed them, they become holy again. If he redeemed them again, they become holy again, until they are cut down. Once they are cut down, he redeems them one time and that is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: בר פדא answers the question. 'No redemption' is not forever. It only means that redeeming does not hold while the saplings are still uncut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow made them holy 'until they are cut,' so as long as they stand, the holiness keeps coming back right after each redemption. That is why the משנה calls them unredeemable. After the cutting, the holiness stops coming back, so one redemption frees them for good.

keyTerms.meaning: An early אמורא who gives the first answer
He redeemed them (paid money to take away their holiness)
And that is enough for him

steps.confusionAlert: 'No redemption' in the משנה does not mean redeeming is forbidden. It means redeeming does not last, because the holiness comes right back while the saplings stand.

phrases.english: Bar Padda said:
If he redeemed them, they become holy again,
if he redeemed them again, they become holy again,
until they are cut down.
Once they are cut down, he redeems them one time, and that is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 by limiting 'no redemption' to the time before the cutting.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not forever. Before cutting, each redemption is undone because the saplings become holy again. After cutting, a single redemption is enough.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before cutting, redemption does not last. After cutting, one redemption is required and is enough.

steps.title: עולא: After cutting, no redemption is needed at all
steps.stepSummary: עולא disagrees with בר פדא. Once the saplings are cut, they need no redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא said: Once they are cut down, he does not need to redeem them again.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a different view about what happens after the cutting. He says no redemption is needed then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר פדא and עולא agree that before the cutting, redemption does not last. They disagree about after the cutting. בר פדא says one more redemption is needed. עולא says the holiness simply ends when the time limit of 'until they are cut' is reached, so there is nothing left to redeem.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who disagrees with בר פדא
Once they have been cut down
He no longer redeems them; no further redemption is needed

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that before the cutting, redemption does not hold. After the cutting, בר פדא requires one redemption, while עולא says the holiness has simply ended and no redemption is needed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows two ways of seeing a time-limited holiness: either it still needs one final redemption, or it simply ends on its own when the time limit is reached.

phrases.english: And Ulla said:
Once they are cut down, he no longer needs to redeem them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer that disagrees with בר פדא about the stage after the cutting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the saplings are cut, they are no longer holy and need no redemption.
